text: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable abilities in various NLP tasks. They are trained on amassive amount of data, often large parts of the internet, and are able to generate human like responses tonatural language inputs on a level that can rival human answers [6]. Especially ChatGPT, an LLM chatbotmade available to the public, has seen an explosion in usage, passing a 100 million monthly users in just ayear [12]. It is already commonly used amongst students.The quality of LLM responses often depends on the use of specific prompting techniques [7]. In this technique,the trained LLMs are provided with specific inputs to act as a guideline for generating the desired output.Moreover, LLMs can be aligned during training, steering their output in a desired direction [14]. As thisprocess is very involved in the training, this approach is rarely used for achieving specific behaviours and actsas a larger-picture guideline for models to behave human-like. While prompting has been widely studied, thisstudy explores its application in a novel context.
